record.paper_title: Descriptions of Cantor Sets: A Set-Theoretic Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Establish conditions under which the Cantor-set families arising from the asymmetric-construction problem, the irrational-endpoint problem, the variable-gap deletion problem, and the symmetry-variation problem have a non-empty mutual intersection.

(OP2) Irrational end-points. Find descriptive formulas when the retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing K ≥ 2 IFS components.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following four families of Cantor-type subsets of the unit interval [0,1], each obtained as the limit of an iterative interval-removal procedure:

(F1) Asymmetric IFS Cantor sets. For an integer K ≥ 2, let Φ = {φ_1, …, φ_K} be a finite system of contracting affine maps φ_i(x) = r_i x + s_i with 0 < r_i < 1, whose images φ_i([0,1]) are pairwise disjoint subintervals of [0,1] and such that the configuration {φ_i([0,1])}_{i=1}^K is not invariant under the reflection x ↦ 1−x. Let C(Φ) denote the unique non-empty compact set satisfying C(Φ) = ⋃_{i=1}^K φ_i(C(Φ)).

(F2) Irrational-endpoint Cantor sets. The subfamily of (F1) (with K ≥ 2) for which at least one endpoint of some interval φ_i([0,1]) is irrational.

(F3) Variable-gap middle-deletion Cantor sets. Given a sequence (α_n)_{n≥1} with 0 < α_n < 1 and 1 − ∑_{n=1}^∞ 2^{n−1} α_n ≥ 0, construct C((α_n)) by setting C_0 = [0,1] and, given C_{n−1} as a disjoint union of 2^{n−1} closed intervals of equal length, removing from each the open middle interval of relative length α_n; let C((α_n)) = ⋂_{n≥0} C_n.

(F4) Symmetry-controlled Cantor sets. The subfamily of (F3) further parameterized by whether each stage's removed middle interval is required to be centrally symmetric within its parent component or is allowed to be off-center by a prescribed offset.

Let 𝓕_1, 𝓕_2, 𝓕_3, 𝓕_4 denote the four families above, viewed as collections of subsets of [0,1].

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters defining the four families under which the intersection 𝓕_1 ∩ 𝓕_2 ∩ 𝓕_3 ∩ 𝓕_4 is non-empty; that is, characterize when there exists a Cantor set C ⊂ [0,1] simultaneously realizable as a member of all four families.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a synthesis of four open problems concerning descriptive formulas for Cantor sets generated by asymmetric IFSs, irrational endpoints, variable middle-gap deletions, and symmetry variations. No published resolution of the joint intersection question was located; the constituent problems are stated as open.
